other_opex.text: Other operating expense was $33 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $3 million or 9% compared with the third quarter of 2025. For the first nine months of 2026, other operating expense was $108 million, a decrease of $3 million or 2% compared with the first nine months of 2025. The decreases were mainly due to legal expense recoveries associated with the resolution of problem loans.

prov.heading: Allowance for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The allowance for credit losses represents management’s estimate of expected credit losses of financial assets measured at amortized cost and certain off-balance sheet credit exposures. Additional information regarding the Company’s allowance for credit losses methodology, significant judgments and assumptions is provided in Item 7. MD&A — Critical Accounting Estimates and Item 8. Financial Statements — Note 1 — Summary of Significant Accounting Policies to the Consolidated Financial Statements in the Company’s 2025 Form 10-K, and Note 6 — Loans Receivable and Allowance for Credit Losses to the Consolidated Financial Statements in this Form 10-Q.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table presents the components of noninterest expense for the third quarters and first nine months of 2026 and 2025:

Noninterest expense was $283 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $6 million or 2% compared with the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher amortization of tax credit and CRA investments, computer- and software-related expense, occupancy and equipment expense, and deposit insurance premiums and regulatory assessments. These increases were partially offset by lower compensation and employee benefits, lower other operating expense, improved OREO results, and decreases in certain other noninterest expense categories. For the first nine months of 2026, noninterest expense was $854 million, an increase of $69 million or 9% compared with the first nine months of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher compensation and employee benefits, amortization of tax credit and CRA investments, computer- and software-related expense, and occupancy and equipment expense, partially offset by improved OREO results and decreases in certain other noninterest expense categories.

Compensation and employee benefits were $170 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $6 million or 3% compared with the third quarter of 2025.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The following table presents income before income taxes, income tax expense and the effective tax rate for the third quarters and first nine months of 2026 and 2025:

Income tax expense was $113 million for the third quarter of 2026, resulting in an effective tax rate of 22.7%, compared with $97 million and an effective tax rate of 20.8% for the same period in 2025. For the first nine months of 2026, income tax expense was $316 million, and the effective tax rate was 22.3%, compared with $290 million and 23.0%, respectively, for the same period in 2025. The increase in income tax expense for both periods was primarily driven by higher pre-tax income, while the three month period additionally reflected lower tax benefits from tax credits. The increase for the nine month period further reflected the partial derecognition of a purchased tax credit in 2026, partially offset by the release of valuation allowance associated with foreign tax credits. Income tax expense and effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 also reflected the impact of a one-time revaluation of deferred tax assets resulting from the adoption of California’s revised state tax apportionment methodology.

net.text: The Company’s net income for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 of $382 million and $1.1 billion, respectively, increased $14 million or 4%, and $135 million or 14%, respectively, from the corresponding periods in 2025. The year-over-year increase in net income for the third quarter of 2026 was primarily attributable to higher net interest income before provision for credit losses, partially offset by higher income tax expense and provision for credit losses. The year-over-year increase in net income for the first nine months of 2026 was primarily driven by higher net interest income before provision for credit losses and noninterest income, and lower provision for credit losses, partially offset by increases in noninterest expense and income tax expense. wc.text: The C&I loan portfolio supports a broad range of commercial customers through diverse commercial business lending, working capital lines of credit, trade finance, letters of credit, asset-based lending, asset-backed finance, project finance, equipment financing and other commercial banking products. The majority of the C&I loans had variable interest rates as of both September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
The Company’s primary source of revenue is net interest income, which is the difference between interest income earned on interest-earning assets and interest expense paid on interest-bearing liabilities. Net interest margin is calculated as net interest income divided by average interest-earning assets. Net interest income and net interest margin are impacted by factors such as changes in the volume and composition of interest-earning assets and funding sources, market interest rates, the slope of the yield curve, the repricing characteristics and maturity profile of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, the level of noninterest-bearing funding sources and asset quality.

Net interest income increased year-over-year for both the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, primarily reflecting higher average loan balances, lower funding costs on interest-bearing deposits, and higher average AFS debt securities balances. These increases were partially offset by lower yields on loans, interest-bearing cash and deposits with banks, and AFS debt securities. Net interest margin declined year-over-year in the third quarter of 2026, primarily due to lower asset yields, partially offset by the benefit of lower interest-bearing deposit funding costs.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
The following table presents the components of noninterest income for the third quarters and first nine months of 2026 and 2025:

Noninterest income was $104 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $3 million or 3% from the third quarter of 2025. T he increase was primarily driven by higher commercial and consumer deposit-related fees, foreign exchange income, and favorable customer derivative income and derivative mark-to-market adjustments, partially offset by lower other income. Noninterest income was $313 million for the first nine months of 2026, an increase of $34 million or 12% from the first nine months of 2025. The increase primarily reflected higher wealth management, commercial and consumer deposit-related fees, and foreign exchange income, partially offset by lower other income.

Commercial and consumer deposit-related fees were $33 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $4 million or 15% from the third quarter of 2025. For the first nine months of 2026, commercial and consumer deposit-related fees were $95 million, an increase of $12 million or 15% from the first nine months of 2025. These increases reflected higher commercial customer activity.

Foreign exchange income was $18 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $3 million or 23% from the third quarter of 2025.

intro.text: East West is a bank holding company incorporated in Delaware on August 26, 1998, and is registered under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (“BHC Act”). The Company commenced business on December 30, 1998 when, pursuant to a reorganization, it acquired all of the voting stock of East West Bank (“East West Bank” or the “Bank”), which became its principal asset. East West’s principal business is to serve as a holding company for the Bank and other banking or banking-related subsidiaries that East West may establish or acquire. As of December 31, 2025, the Company had $80.4 billion in total assets, $56.1 billion in total net loans, $67.1 billion in total deposits, and $8.9 billion in total stockholders’ equity.

accounts.name: Investments
accounts.note: Securities bought and sold sit in 'other investing' with everything else the section does not name.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
